descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Algebra (Modelling) — Mathematical Modelling at the Sugar Bush (C4)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Grade-1 unit on mathematical modelling (C4) framed around the Canadian sugar bush — Maple the Maple Tree and Sap Sam the Collector. Children walk through the 5-step modelling cycle from real-life situations to predictions and refinements.
long_description: Children spend a focused week as Junior Mathematical Modellers. Day 1 introduces situations and math questions (C4 step 1). Day 2 collects data (C4 step 2). Day 3 predicts using rules (C4 step 3). Day 4 reflects and refines (C4 step 4). Day 5 closes with child-chosen capstone modelling projects (C4 integrated). Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough covering misconceptions: descriptive-vs-mathematical questions, data-without-table, over-confident predictions, wrong-vs-imperfect framing, and choice paralysis.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans with 50-minute durations and 250 minutes of total teaching time
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson

10 printable teacher manipulatives plus 2 character puppets: paper maple trees (20), sap buckets (20), modelling cycle chart, data collection table, prediction chart, capstone template, real-life situation cards (12), two-colour counters, syrup jar template, sugar bush anchor poster, plus stick-puppet variants of Maple and Sap Sam
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 self-assessment prompts
1 single-row summative rubric covering C4 across 4 levels
1 summative-administration guide tying the rubric to Lesson 5 capstone
Junior Mathematical Modeller certificate (one per child)
Detailed expanded walkthroughs covering common misconceptions
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson
target_buyer: Ontario Grade 1 teachers covering the C4 cluster — mathematical modelling for real-life situations.
subject: Mathematics
pedagogical_approach: CRA progression. The sugar bush poster and modelling cycle chart are the anchors — children walk through the 5 steps physically. Lesson 1 conceptualises situations and questions. Lesson 2 collects data. Lesson 3 predicts. Lesson 4 reflects and refines. Lesson 5 closes with child-chosen capstone projects modelled on situations from their own lives.
